Titanium limbs: Life-changing engineering meets anatomy

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Engineering meets anatomy when you say Dr George Vicatos - his state-of-the-art limb designs are changing lives and his international claim to fame is that he made the largest ever implant worldwide. Every person’s pelvis is a unique design and shape and when you need a replacement you can't pick a modular pelvis designed off the shelf. George designs precision replicas of your unique bone structure which is 3D printed with medical titanium in a state-of-the-art unit in Bloemfontein Technicon at the Centre of Rapid Prototyping and Manufacturing (CRPM). It’s a good news story with top South African surgeons working closely with the designers and academics making life-changing surgery available to South Africans at one third of the price and in half the manufacturing time, and Vicatos ensures he attends every surgery.. The day before the surgery he sits with the doctor and a nylon replica of the implant making any last-minute adjustments. Vicatos really takes to heart the enormity of the life-changing surgery for every patients. The best news is that the Medical Aids are on board.

Summary:
Like a bolt out of the blue, Mark Jonkers’ life was shattered, the last thing he remembers was being parked at a 4-way stop in Somerset West. He woke to a shattered pelvis and in excruciating pain which never went away for the next 18 months, he was trapped in a wheelchair and at the age of 37 was told he would never walk again. But thanks to the incredible combined skills of mechanical engineer Dr George Vicatos and orthopaedic surgeon Dr Andre Olivier the pain is gone and Mark is walking and dedicating his life to changing kids’ lives.
Mark's previous surgeon spent months sending his scans to many different international prosthesis manufacturers and every solution they came up with was too risky, then he was referred to Dr Andre Olivier and four weeks later he had a new pelvis and hip. Today he is walking and the pain has gone, along with the 22 screws that were holding him together after the initial emergency surgery.
The complex thing about a pelvis is because it is the weight-bearing centre of our bodies to which our limbs are anchored, you can’t just add modular pieces, it has to be a solid structure that mirrors your exact pelvis. Technological advancements in computer design and 3D manufacturing with advanced medical scans all married together with highly skilled surgeons, has put South Africa on the world stage of medical science.





Further information:
Apart from trauma, bone tumours are the other cause of massive pelvis transplants. And because cancer can grow rapidly in the body, the quicker it is removed the better, and so the fact that an implant can be manufactured in 15 days is life changing. In the past, people would have limbs amputated and had to be satisfied with the fact they had survived cancer. Today they can regain full mobility. Bone cancer can advance rapidly and so in his design George has to accommodate the potential changes from the moment the scan is done until surgery is possible. George has invested in The Centre of Rapid Prototyping and Manufacturing (CRPM) in Bloemfontein where the 3D printing is done with medical titanium.

Press Release:


Titanium Implants
Imagine having an acute type of bone cancer, so debilitating you’ll need your pelvis to be scraped and shaped to fit a new prosthesis. But there’s a real problem - off-the-shelf artificial implants for pelvic repair often don’t succeed. But to be mobile again, that’s the only choice you have - at least that used to be the case. Now, using innovative medical techniques, mechanical engineers, designers and orthopaedic surgeons can combine their skills to 3D-print your unique bone structure in medical titanium. Custom-built to fit individual patient needs, these titanium implants are changing the lives of transplant patients.
Producer: Liz Fish | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


Script: Tucked away down a dark corridor at UCT, Biomechanical engineer George Vicatos, often sits through the night designing implants that are changing people's lives.

George: At the end of the line is a patient waiting. And you cannot you cannot play with that particular time.

Script: Born from his love of anatomy and his excellence in engineering, he ensures they are able to handle the stresses and strains that bones endure. The implants are 3D printed out of medical titanium at the Centre of Rapid Prototyping and Manufacturing in Bloemfontein. In just over two weeks, orthopaedic surgeons are able to operate with these individualised implants, transforming the lives of people like Duan Brink

Duan “I couldn't cross my one leg over the other and I struggled to start walking and my wife suggested I go do some yoga. And I said I'd rather go and see a physio

Link “When a little stiffness in your hip turns out to be a massive cancerous tumour in your pelvis that is pretty terrifying especially when you have two young boys to raise

Duan “I was able to walk but I couldn't run anymore. And I used to be a strong runner. ...I couldn't even play soccer with my kids. And that made me realize that I had to do something about it cause I couldn't continue like this

Script: Just months ago, Johannesburg chartered account Duan Brink underwent an 18 hour operation to remove a rare cancerous tumour that couldn’t be treated with either chemo or radiation. It was growing through his hip socket, explains orthopaedic surgeon Dr Richard Kyte.

Richard “Cancers are a bit like a bit like a creeper. They creep along blood vessels and nerves and they actually do it very clean in a very clandestine way so you can’t see it you can't define them. The more aggressive tumors will double in three to six weeks time.

Script: It was an extremely complex operation and potentially life threatening

Duan “I'm going to leave my kids, potentially alone with my wife but I made it and I am here and I am here and every day I look forward to spending time with them
Script: Duan pulled through, and his operation was a success

Script: Pelvic tumours and trauma have the most devastating impact on people, leaving them immobile and in crippling pain. They are also the most difficult bones to access and fix, explains orthopaedic surgeon Dr Andre Olivier
Masa “ is repairing a pelvis more complicated than other bones

Andre “Yes, indeed. The problem with the pelvis is the 3D anatomy. It's extremely difficult to reconstruct that. It differs from patient to patient. And if there is a big defect for either tumor patient or patient, 2 had 3 or four previous operations and there is now a big gap in the pelvis to reconstruct that is very difficult because of the anatomy.

Script: The pelvis houses the bladder, bowel and genitalia, as well as the major nerves and blood supply to the legs, all of which have to be navigated around. Every pelvis is unique, so if off the shelf implants are used, it can leave people with one leg shorter, and less mobile.

George “you cannot design something and expect the surgeon to just plonk it in put it in the pelvis. You have to design something that can actually bypass all the structures, not to injure them. And that is the difficult part.

Script: Once George has the CT scan of the patient he designs a implant that is the exact replica of their bone, taking into account where the surgeon wants to attach it

George” So I took the correct side the good side, mirrored it and now I have symmetry of the hip, and now on this particular part I build the implant which is that

Script: One of the most critical aspects of George’s designs is a gig, which shows the surgeon exactly where he decided to cut, and where to anchor the implant.

Richard “ And we can practice, if you like, making sure that the position that this fits is exact because it can any fit in it in one plane which allows us then to pin and cut the pelvis exactly as one needs to it's actually impossible to do this operation successfully and reliably without such a jig.

Link: “After a freak car accident at the age of 37 Mark Jonker was told he would never walk again after 18 months in a wheelchair in extreme pain he was losing hope

Mark “It felt like you took a Taser, literally an electric Taser at the bottom of my foot. Twenty four hours a day. And on the top of my foot felt like you took a cheese grater to it 24 hours a day

Script: He lost his job and if it wasn’t for his family, he would have been destitute, but he was determined to find help. One orthopaedic surgeon spent months looking suitable implants from overseas suppliers, but none were viable

Mark “George was the first person that actually had a breakthrough and had a solution,

Masa “How remarkable that is that you had options from abroad and right here back there was a solution.

Mark “That was unbelievable. I mean, in Cape Town, [06:22:35] And with all of these thoughts of European doctors almost superior that the more technology they've got, all these things that we don't have in South Africa. So it was quite a surprise that it was actually in my backyard less than 50 kms from where I am staying
Andre “The important thing is that we can do it locally. That is a massive cost saving for us. If we looked at we've we've tried that route before to import these implants, but to get them the customs clearance, the medical aid to pay for these. It's not easy and it takes a very long time
Script: Infection is one of the biggest problems with all implants. Japie Diedricks had four hip replacements and after the last op they told him there was nothing more they could
do. At the age of 27, having just run the comrades and was training to be a professional cyclist, a head on collision stripped him of his mobility, and at times - his sanity

Japie” Sometimes you feel like, why keep on living? Why don't you stop living I was at a stage I couldn’t handle it anymore,

Andre “Eventually they couldn't do a hip replacement for him anymore. And the simple reason is that you don’t have fixation points to do a normal hip replacement if there's not enough bone stock left

Japie “ If I had to go and sit or come and visit you, I nearly had to lie back in the sofa and that my leg had to be straight in it. If I won now, I can sit nearly normal in it. It’s much easier

Script: What’s ground-breaking here, is the close collaboration between the surgeons and the designer right up to the point of inserting the implant. George even ensure he meets the patient just before they go under

Richard “If you're collaborating with someone overseas, almost always you don't even know the designer. You're not sure what product you're getting, with George not only do you know what product you're getting, he is in theatre and he's making jolly certain that it works.

Masa “What drives you George because you are doing this over and above your academic commitments

George “Yes, I do. I'm full, full time academic this is my night time. And what actually makes my day is that my design has a function very, very quickly into someone's body.Not being whole again as before, but having it almost natural life again
Script: And for these patients - it’s nothing short of miraculous

Mark So the feeling of being able to to work again, to contribute again is a massive relief

Duan “ I 'm very positive. I think probably less about the future. And I'm a lot more present in the moment with my kids, with my wife and I pulled through and I am so relieved
